resources.string: Running on a TV: it will connect to this device itself.
Running on a phone: it will connect to a TV over the network.
Cannot reach the device. Check that it is on the same network and that debugging is enabled.
The device needs pairing with a code. Open Wireless debugging on it and use pairing below.
Confirm the debugging prompt on the device screen, then try again.
The device rejected the pairing code. Codes expire quickly — open a fresh one.
Pairing timed out. Check the network and request a fresh pairing code.
Pairing could not finish. Check the pairing port and request a fresh code on the TV.
The secure connection could not be established. Check the debugging port and try again.
Pairing requires Android 10 or later on the device running this app. Classic network debugging is still available.
Connection failed for an unexpected reason.
On the TV open Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code.
The pairing port and the connection port are different. Both are shown on the TV.
Devices found automatically on the network
No devices found. Make sure wireless debugging is on and its screen is open.
Network discovery is unavailable on this device. Enter the address manually.
Network discovery could not start on this device: %1$s. Enter the address manually — everything else works.
Allow local network access to discover TVs and connect to their addresses.
Search by country code, country name or address — for example ru, by, kz. Case does not matter. Tapping a result puts the address into the field below.
A domain name (time.google.com) or an IP address (216.239.35.0) — both work.
IP: %1$s — tap to use the address instead of the name
That is not a valid server address.
The device still reports %1$s. The connection may not have permission to change secure settings.
Could not change the time server: %1$s
When connecting for the first time, the TV asks to allow debugging from this device and shows a key fingerprint. Confirm it on the TV screen — ticking “Always allow” saves you from repeating it.
Answers as a time server: %1$d ms, %2$d%% of replies, clock offset %3$s s.
Does not answer as a time server: %1$s
It answers, but reports a time that is far off. Applying it would break the clock rather than fix it.
No server answered. The network may be blocking NTP.
The app closed unexpectedly last time. Details:\n%1$s
